title: A Wild Sprint Stantler Hops the Route 29 signpost from rest

verification.actor: One prepared current Wild Stantler (species 234) idle at map 33 tile (580,397), with the resolved Sprint lane and attached presentation
verification.trigger: At the common Wild direction-choice entry, choose East for one obstacle request from (580,397); leave the stock collision and motion code unchanged
verification.observable: One two-tile Hop crosses the static blocked signpost at (581,397), lands at (582,397), and returns control. Native terrain reports an open takeoff and landing tile.

setupMutations.change: Use a disposable save, checked map 33 teleport to player (584,397), native Wild Stantler spawn at (580,397), and exact-subject bind.
The bounded native control changes only r1 to East at one Wild direction-choice call from (580,397). It does not write game memory, force a return value, change the Sprint lane or admit a motion.

limits: This controlled direction choice proves the shared Wild caller and Sprint movement policy for one static obstacle. It does not prove a planned Walk-to-Hop route, natural Wander RNG, Chase targeting, Flee targeting or natural population spawning.

A prior two-step controlled test changed the candidate direction after the caller computed its turn permission. It therefore did not represent one coherent planned route; this case starts idle beside the obstacle.
Copied-data controls reject false terrain, changed actor, altered direction register, wrong start, short Hop and missing Hop commit. Registration alone is not accepted runtime proof.

events.value: Place the player near the signpost, spawn and bind Wild Sprint Stantler idle at (580,397)
Arm the bounded East direction control at the shared Wild step entry
Observe one two-tile Hop and its terminal commit under neutral input
Close the control after the two-tile landing

stop.condition: The same Stantler commits one two-tile Hop at (582,397)

invariants: Only the candidate direction register is changed; the game still accepts or rejects each motion
The takeoff tile is open, the next tile is a static collision, and the two-tile landing is open
The Hop commits exactly once on the same current actor
The trace and completed game frames remain contiguous without a canceled motion
